title: US govt may soon increase H-1B and L-1 visas fees for large companies
content: The US government plans to expand an additional fee for certain visa petitions. This fee currently applies to initial H-1B and L-1 visa grants. The proposed change will extend this charge to petitions for extensions of stay. Companies with over fifty employees and a majority on these visas will be affected. This expansion aims to fund biometric entry-exit systems and other government programs.

title: Former Pakistan cricketers face possible PCB ban: Here's why

The PCB emphasized the importance of obtaining necessary approvals for international participation.

title: Insect-eating plant proves Darwin’s 150-year-old theory right
content: A breakthrough in plant science has validated Charles Darwin's historic conjecture surrounding carnivorous Saxifraga species. Researchers discovered that these plants ensnare small gnats with sticky hairs, emitting fragrances that lure their prey. Chemical tests confirmed that insects provide essential nutrients upon capture, as showcased by isotope labeling. This pivotal finding sheds light on the complex interactions and nutritional strategies of plant carnivory in mountainous regions.

title: Bombardier beetle carries its own chemical bomb against predators
content: Bombardier beetles possess a unique defense mechanism involving explosive chemical sprays.  These insects mix chemicals to create a hot, noxious spray for protection.  Their specialized internal structures allow them to survive these powerful self-inflicted explosions.  Bombardier beetles can fire their chemical bombs multiple times before needing to escape.  These fascinating insects have evolved remarkable adaptations for survival in various ecosystems.

title: Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding
content: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. This school provided education, healthcare, and family support to low-income children. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative will not continue funding beyond the upcoming academic year. Academic results remained below state averages, prompting the board's decision. The initiative pledged fifty million dollars to aid the transition for affected students.

title: Heavens won’t fall if all 6 Vande stanzas sung in madrassas: Calcutta HC
content: The Calcutta High Court heard a public interest litigation challenging mandatory Vande Mataram stanzas.  The court questioned the necessity of forcing students to sing specific religious or nationalistic songs.  Arguments were made that forcing the song could disrupt communal harmony and lead to legal issues.  The court noted that no coercive steps have been taken regarding the notification yet.  Additional Solicitor General opposed the interim prayer, calling some PILs publicity-driven.

title: Australia gamble on no warm-up games ahead of five-Test BGT 2027

This preparation phase will kick off following their concluding home series against New Zealand. Depending on local conditions, squad choices for the Indian tour might change. Fans can mark their calendars—the five-Test series launches in Nagpur on January 21, 2027.

title: IndiGo ordered to pay Rs 60K after passenger misses flight
content: A consumer commission found IndiGo liable for service deficiency after a passenger missed his flight. The airline failed to provide complete terminal information on the ticket and SMS. This omission caused the passenger to go to the wrong terminal and miss his flight. The commission ordered IndiGo to pay compensation and litigation costs to the passenger.

title: Government may allow fees on UPI payment above Rs 2,000
content: The government may allow a small charge on UPI payments exceeding two thousand rupees. This levy would apply to transactions made to businesses and not individuals.  Official estimates suggest this change will impact only five percent of all UPI transactions.  Most daily purchases like groceries and taxi fares will remain unaffected by this potential fee.  Industry experts anticipate a possible ceiling on the absolute amount charged for these transactions.

title: As France sees its first fire cloud, should India be worried?
content: France witnessed its first pyrocumulonimbus fire cloud event in July 2026.  This phenomenon occurs when intense wildfires create their own thunderstorms.  India's rising temperatures and dry spells increase forest fire frequency.  While India has not reported fire clouds, its forests are becoming more flammable.  The Himalayan pine belt presents the highest potential for such an event in India.

title: 'You told Sooryavanshi to serve water': Ex-India star questions his debut timing

Authorities recovered illegal firearms, petrol bombs, and a stolen motorcycle from the arrested suspects.  The accused were reportedly recruiting local youth for terror activities and conducting surveillance.  These individuals acted at the behest of handlers from the Inter-Services Intelligence agency. Nearly nineteen lakh households now receive zero electricity bills, reducing their costs.  Over twelve lakh households earned money by selling surplus solar power back.  The program also supports low-income families and creates jobs nationwide.

These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to ISRO facilities. The programs are designed to lower entry barriers and accelerate private sector growth. This support will make satellite data and infrastructure more affordable for Indian entities.
